pairs.difference: A Hospital is big, has wards and an emergency department; a Clinic is one doctor's small practice.
A Hotel has private rooms and room service; a Hostel has shared dorms and is cheap, for backpackers or students.
At a Library you borrow books and keep quiet; at a Bookshop you buy them.
A Bank does loans, cards and accounts; a Post Office sends letters and parcels (and also keeps savings accounts).
A Salon is for hair and grooming; a Spa is for massages and relaxing.
School means uniforms, assemblies and younger kids; College means bunking lectures and no uniform.
A Museum shows history and artefacts; an Art Gallery shows paintings, often for sale.
A Supermarket is big, with trolleys and self-service; a Kirana Store is the small neighbourhood shop where the owner hands you things.
A Pub is for sitting and drinking with friends; a Nightclub is for dancing to loud music until late.
A Food Court is in a mall, with many brand counters; a Canteen is at an office or college and is cheap.
A Mall is indoors, air-conditioned and full of brands; a Market is open-air, crowded, and you bargain.
A Dhaba is a highway eatery with charpais and dal; a Food Truck is a van that serves snacks from a window in the city.
A Bakery sells breads, cakes and puffs; a Sweet Shop sells mithai by the kilo.
A Gym has weights and machines; a Yoga Studio has mats and quiet breathing.
A Bus Stop is a roadside shelter; a Metro Station has turnstiles, escalators and cards.
You file a complaint at a Police Station; you serve a sentence in Jail.
A Zoo has land animals in enclosures; an Aquarium has fish in tanks.
A Bowling Alley has lanes and pins; an Arcade has video games and claw machines.
A Chemist sells medicines; an Optician sells glasses and tests your eyes.
A Stadium is huge, with stands and tickets; a Playground is the local open ground where kids play.
A Café is air-conditioned, with coffee and laptops; a Tea Stall is a roadside spot for cutting chai.
A Flat is one home in a building; a Bungalow is a standalone house with its own garden.
An Airport has flights and security checks; a Railway Station has trains, platforms and coolies.
A Beach has sand, waves and salt water; a Swimming Pool has tiles, lanes and chlorine.
A Fire Station keeps red fire engines ready for emergencies; a Bus Depot is where city buses park and get repaired.
At a Petrol Pump you fill fuel; at a Car Wash you get the car cleaned.
At a Cinema you sit in the dark watching a film; at an Amusement Park you go on rides all day.
A Construction Site is outdoors, building something new with cranes and cement; a Warehouse is a big shed where goods are stored and loaded onto trucks.
A Garden is on the ground, with grass and plants; a Terrace is the rooftop of a building.
A Flyover lifts the road over traffic; a Railway Crossing is where the road meets the tracks, with gates that drop when a train comes.
